Challenging judgment and award dated 02.11.2017 passed by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Kalaburagi (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC no.826/2015, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and M.A.C.T., Kalaburagi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Sri B. Ali Mohammad, learned counsel for appellant submitted that, appeal was by claimant for enhancement.

It was further submitted that since insurer had not challenged award and only claimant was in appeal, finding of Tribunal about occurrence of accident involving insured vehicle due to rash and negligent driving by its driver, coverage as on date of accident and liability of insurer to pay compensation are not in dispute.
It was submitted that claimant aged 20 years and earning NC: 2023:KHC-K:6459 Rs.12,000/- per month as coolie, sustained fracture of left humerus and fracture of superior and inferior pubic rami.
It was submitted that Tribunal considered lower monthly income of Rs.6,000/- while assessing compensation.
Even disability considered was on lower side.
Further, award of Rs.5,000/- towards pain and suffering, Rs.5,000/- towards loss of amenities was inadequate.
No compensation was awarded towards loss of income during laid-up period.
On above grounds, sought for allowing appeal.
3. On other hand, Sm. Preeti Patil Melkundi, learned counsel for respondent no.2 sought to support impugned award.

4. Heard learned counsel and perused impugned judgment and award and copy of wound certificates and X- ray report - Exs.P5 & P6 and P11 made available by learned counsel for claimant.
5.

From above submission and since only claimant was in appeal for enhancement, point that arises for consideration is:

sentences.text: Though claimant stated that he was earning Rs.12,000/- per month as coolie, same is not substantiated with evidence.
In absence, same has to be assessed notionally.
Notional income for year 2013 (date of accident) is Rs.7,000/-.
Therefore, same has to be considered.
PW.2-Dr.Ravi examined claimant and issued disability certificate - Ex.P10 assessing disability at 30%.
Tribunal considered it at 10%.
From Exs.P5 and P6, fracture of humerus and pubic rami are established.
PW.2 opined that there was malunion.
Considering age and occupation, disability assessed cannot be stated to be grossly inadequate.

Thus, future loss of income would be:
Rs.7,000/- x 10% x 12 x 16 = Rs.1,34,400/-
7.
Since claimant sustained two grievous fractures, award of Rs.5,000/- towards pain and suffering would be grossly inadequate.
It would be appropriate to NC: 2023:KHC-K:6459 enhance it to Rs.60,000/-.
Against medical bills produced for Rs.6,900/-, Tribunal awarded said amount, which would be appropriate.
Normally, fractures take about three months to heal.
Therefore, it would be appropriate to award Rs.21,000/- (Rs.7,000 x 3) towards loss of income during laid-up period.
Claimant sustained grievous fractures, which were malunited.
In view of same, it would be appropriate to award Rs.30,000/- towards loss of amenities.
Rs.5,000/- awarded towards above head has to be considered as towards incidental expenses.
Thus, claimant would be entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,57,300/-.
8. Point for consideration is answered accordingly.

Consequently, following:
ORDER i. Appeal is allowed-in-part with costs.

ii. Claimant is held entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,57,300/- with interest at 6% p.a. from date of claim petition till deposit.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:6459 iii. Respondent no.2-insurer is directed to deposit enhanced amount with interest within a period of six weeks from date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
iv. On deposit, entire enhanced amount with interest shall be released in favour of claimant.
